tagline.text: The southeastern beach town that holds Bantayan Island's gateway port and white-sand resorts

location.label: Location
location.text: Southeastern Bantayan Island, Cebu Province, around Santa Fe Port

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: 2 days and 1 night to 3 days and 2 nights

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱2,000–4,500 (per person, for 2 days and 1 night)

children.text: Santa Fe is the gateway town of Bantayan Island, reached by ferry from Hagnaya in Cebu, and the beach resorts and island-hopping boats are concentrated here. It is both the starting point of an island trip and the place where the most travelers stay.

Santa Fe is a municipality at the southeastern end of Bantayan Island, with an area of about 28 km² and about 35,000 residents (2024). Along with the southeastern part of the main island it includes the small islands of Guintacan (Kinatarkan), Hilantagaan and Hilantagaan Diot (Silion), and it has 10 barangays. It borders Bantayan town to the north and west, Medellin to the east and the Tañon Strait to the south. Its economy rests on fishing and farming, and tourism peaks especially around Holy Week. The population, about 34,000 in the 2020 census, has stayed at a similar level in 2024.

There is one reason Santa Fe became the travelers' base. Ferries from Hagnaya (San Remigio) Port and Kawit Port in Medellin on mainland Cebu all dock at its harbor. From the port to a beachfront lodging is about 10 minutes by tricycle, so you can drop your bags and be in the sea right away. Bantayan Airport (runway about 1,200 m) is also in Santa Fe and serves the whole island.

The beaches are known for fine white sand and calm water. They run in a row, including Paradise Beach, Kota Beach and its sandbar, which often appear in photos, Alice Beach, the Maricaban coast, and the southern shore called Sugar Beach. Most resorts look after the beach in front of them and some charge a small entrance fee. There are no Boracay-style beach parties; the mood is quiet and restful.

Island hopping also starts from Santa Fe. The usual route takes a bangka around Virgin Island, Hilantagaan Island and the Baigad (Balidbid) lagoon, and it is finished in half a day. Santa Fe is also known for its sunrise, and many people go to the beach at dawn to watch it. During Holy Week the whole island is crowded with family travelers from all over Cebu.

This is Santa Fe's signature beach, where rock formations run along the shore. Depending on the guide the entrance fee is about ₱50–70, and it is said to be waived on quiet days. The inner sand is peaceful and good for playing in the water with children.

Known as a filming location for a movie, this beach is notable for the small sandbar that appears at low tide. Reviews say non-guests are sometimes charged about ₱50, waived if you eat at the restaurant, while a recent review says there is no entrance fee, so sources differ.

Virgin Island, off Santa Fe, is privately owned and is said to charge a landing fee. One blog gives about ₱500 for 2 people plus about ₱100 for each extra person. Guides say a joiner island-hopping tour costs about ₱1,350 per person including entrance and environmental fees. Hilantagaan Island has shallow water that suits snorkeling with children, and plans change with weather and tide, so follow the boatman's advice.

The limestone cave pool inside Ogtong Cave Resort was once Santa Fe's signature attraction. A notice says it was closed for safety inspection after the September 30, 2025 earthquake, so you need to confirm locally whether it has reopened. Use of the resort's pool and beach is separate.

Santa Fe's eastern coast is known for its sunrise. If you go to the beach at sunrise you can watch the sky turn red. For sunset, the west-side coast on the other side of the island (Bantayan town, Madridejos) is better.

This eco park has a walk through coastal mangrove forest, and depending on the guide the entrance fee is about ₱50. It is good for a light walk in the cool morning, and you can see birds and crabs. Check hours and fees on site.

The island's ring road is flat and has little traffic, so you can see it by motorbike in a day. A day's rental is about ₱300–500, and it is good to continue to the church in Bantayan town and Kota Park in Madridejos.
Santa Fe is the busiest town during Holy Week. Lodging rates rise two to three times and many local families pitch tents on the beach, so the place buzzes. If you want quiet, avoid this period.

items.subtitle: From the port to the beach

children.text: Board a bus to Hagnaya Port at the Cebu North Bus Terminal. It takes about
3–4 hours
Take the ferry to Santa Fe from Hagnaya Port. The crossing takes about
1 hour to 1 hour 30 minutes
After arriving at Santa Fe Port, take a tricycle to your lodging, have lunch and rest on the beach.
Walk the beach near your lodging and have a seafood barbecue for dinner.
On the second morning, go to the beach before dawn for the sunrise.
Take a half-day hopping tour of Virgin Island and Hilantagaan.
After lunch, take the ferry from the port back to Hagnaya and return to Cebu City.

A day trip is tight because of ferry times and transfers. Staying at least one night is recommended, and on days when the sea is rough the return ferry can be canceled, so leave a one-day buffer before any flight home.

items.title: 3 days and 2 nights
items.subtitle: Including a loop of the island

children.text: On the first day, arrive in Santa Fe and relax at Paradise Beach or Kota Beach.
On the second day, rent a motorbike and ride to the church in Bantayan town, Obo-ob mangroves and Kota Park in Madridejos.
Watch the sunset at Kota Park and return to Santa Fe before dark.
On the morning of the third day, go island hopping and take the ferry out in the afternoon.
With Santa Fe as a base, you can reach anywhere on the island in 30–45 minutes by motorbike.
A flight from Manila Ninoy Aquino International Airport to Mactan-Cebu Airport (CEB) takes about
1 hour 20 minutes
, and several airlines fly daily.
The small-plane service between Bantayan Airport (Santa Fe) and Mactan runs on few days and is sometimes suspended. Do not hang your schedule on it and check with the airline first.

Most traveler lodgings cluster on the southern coast within 10 minutes by tricycle of Santa Fe Port. As of June 2026, guides give budget rooms from about ₱600–700 a night, upper-end places such as Ogtong Cave Resort from about ₱2,000, and mid-range beach resorts at ₱2,500–5,000. During Holy Week and holidays they sell out months ahead.

The food centers on seafood. Beach barbecue restaurants weigh fish, squid, shrimp and shellfish and grill them, usually cheaper than in Cebu City. Danggit (dried fish) and dried squid, the island's specialties, can be bought vacuum-packed at shops around the port. Santa Fe has few banks and ATMs, so withdraw cash in Bantayan town beforehand.

Around the port and the market there are small eateries and cafés, and port kiosks sell bread, snacks and water cheaply. Beach resort restaurants charge tourist prices, so try at least one meal at a noodle-soup place or barbecue stall near the port at local prices. Nights are generally quiet, a place to rest to the sound of the sea.
Early morning ferries are more reliable. The last boat differs by company and weekday, so check at Hagnaya first.
During Holy Week ferry tickets sell out easily, so book online or arrive early.
Fees for places like Virgin Island depend on whether the place is privately owned. For hopping, you pay at the Santa Fe tourism office and are assigned a bangka.
When renting a motorbike, check the license, helmet and fuel. Island roads are dark at night, so return to your lodging before sunset.
Some resorts waive the entrance fee if you use their restaurant, so ask at the entrance first.
Do not leave trash on the beach, and do not step on or touch the coral.
Carry plenty of cash. Few places in Santa Fe accept cards.
The Santa Fe tourism office (the municipality's tourism department) helps with hopping fees and bangka assignment. Get the latest contact number from your lodging.
After the September 30, 2025 northern Cebu earthquake, some facilities around the port and coast may still be under repair. Boarding at Hagnaya Port is restricted depending on the tide.
Notices say Ogtong Cave closed after the earthquake, so ask the resort before you go whether it is open.
Even though the island roads are flat, there are dogs, chickens and sandy stretches, so ride carefully. Wear a helmet.
Some waters off Santa Fe have strong currents. Wear a life vest when hopping and follow your guide's instructions.
Airport service is irregular. Plan important schedules around the land and sea route through Cebu City.
Lodging prices rise two to three times during Holy Week and holidays.
